Finally, highly connected phylotypes within ecological networks were found to be especially important for maintaining multiple ecosystem functions. Together, our research represents an important step for soil biology and ecosystem ecology. Our collective results suggest that multiple ecosystem functions and services that are supported by soil biodiversity should not be overlooked, as they probably have key roles for human wellbeing and ecosystem sustainability. Locally and across biomes, increasing knowledge of soil biodiversity could provide an emerging cornerstone for biodiversity, conservation and, with time, become a key component of management decision making.

(noch) von weiteren Prozessen überlagert wird.

If peat contains high concentrations of P, pore water and surface water quality become adverse after rewetting due to the mobilization of P as a result of microbial Fe reduction. As reduced Fe compounds are less able to bind P, waterlogging or flooding will always lead to mobilization of Fe-bound P (Ponnamperuma, 1984; Lamers et al., 1998 a ; Zak et al., 2010). The rate of mobilization is determined by the fertilization history of the soils involved, in addition to the type of nutrient binding in the soil (Fig. 3). As Ca- and Al-bound iron P fractions are not redox sensitive, these P reservoirs will not respond to flooding. Post-rewetting, eutrophication is one of the major issues of former agricultural lands and for the restoration of surface waters (lakes, canals, ditches, peat extraction pits) in these areas, but advantageous management techniques can alleviate this problem to ensure successful rich fen restoration. The eutrophying impact of adjacent intensive farming has to be eliminated, which can be a challenge for small-scale restoration projects in agricultural areas. This includes water-quality control, by choosing the best option for water supply and by hydrological uncoupling of adjacent fertilized areas (Richardson et al., 2011). Such control may be difficult, as fen areas have always been used as a buffer in order to keep optimal agricultural hydrological regimes to prevent waterlogging or desiccation. In the Everglades, excess inputs of P from the northern agricultural areas constrain ecological restoration (Richardson, 2010). german_name.evidence_anchor: In contrast, it is able to compete naturally and find its ecological niche (Bauhus et al., 2017) in stands with distinctive and extreme site conditions, e.g. under extreme aridity, on clay soils or floodplains. These natural monospecific oak stands are rare and hardly to find in their optimum growth. In Germany, for example, it can be assumed that almost all monospecific oak stands have been created by human activity on sites with favourable growing conditions (Krahl-Urban, 1959). Consequently, when oak is grown in mixture on the most suitable sites for the species, silvicultural strategies are essential to maintain it as a component of the stand. Oak is traditionally artificially regenerated in many parts of Central Europe and mixed with shade-tolerant tree species introduced at later successional stages to improve its wood quality (Lüpke, 1998; Schutz, 1993). The admixture of European beech, in particular as a subsidiary tree species, is a widely established practice in oak management and the subject of several studies (Bontemps et al., 2012; Dolos et al., 2016; Lupke, 1998; Mette et al., 2013).

german_name.evidence_anchor: Under hypertrophic conditions, phytoplankton reached a mean total biovolume of 17.4 mm³ L⁻¹ in spring (March to May) and 15.9 mm³ L⁻¹ in summer (June to September). By the eutrophic period, the mean biovolume had declined to 4.2 (spring) and 7.2 mm³ L⁻¹ (summer, see Fig. 3). The long-term data sets were divided into three periods: the hypertrophic period from 1979 to 1990, a eutrophic period from 1997 to 2003 and a transient period from 1991 to 1996. Linear regressions were applied to seasonal or annual means each calculated from a large number of individual samples (N > 30), assuming that these aggregated values approximately met requirements for regression analysis. In addition, linear regressions were applied to independent single events such as timing of the spring peak. Data sets were compared using one-way ANOVA and subsequent Tukey tests. The statistical package SPSS 9.0 was used.

Total phosphorus loading declined by 52% and TN loading by 68% as the lakes changed from hypertrophic to eutrophic conditions. One reason for these declines was the reduced inflow into the lake (Table 1). During the hypertrophic period, the TP concentration of the inflowing River Spree averaged 153 lg L⁻¹ in spring (March to May) and 145 lg TP L⁻¹ in summer (June to September). It declined mainly in the transient phase (1991–96). The reduction was more pronounced in spring (≈33%) than in summer (≈12%, Table 2). Mean TN concentrations in the inflow amounted to 3700 lg L⁻¹ (spring) and 2090 lg L⁻¹ (summer) during the hypertrophic period. After a continuous decline only 47% of the initial concentrations were found in the inflow of Müggelsee in both spring and summer of the eutrophic phase.

In the lake, the mean concentration of TN declined by about 50% from the hypertrophic to eutrophic period, but annual mean TP concentrations did not decrease. More important than the annual means, however, are the nutrient concentrations in distinct periods during the growing season. Mean spring TP concentrations averaged 106 lg L⁻¹ in 1979–90 and declined by 10% in 1991–96 and by 33% until 1997–2003. Because of enhanced P release from the sediments, the mean summer TP concentration increased from 231 lg L⁻¹ in the hypertrophic period by 10% during the transient state, and declined only recently by 20% in the eutrophic period (Fig. 1). In the first summers after the loading reduction, the lake acted as a net source of P. Afterwards, net P retention recurred, but to a lesser extent than was the case during the hypertrophic period. In contrast to TP, mean TN concentrations declined steadily not only in spring but also in summer (see Table 2; Fig. 1).

In the inflowing River Spree, the mean TN : TP ratio in spring decreased from 24 in the hypertrophic to 17 during the eutrophic period. In summer, the corresponding ratios were 14 and eight. From inflow to lake, the mean TN : TP ratio slightly increased in spring of all periods but declined further in summer (to eight in the hypertrophic and six in the eutrophic periods). Monthly mean TN : TP ratios <7.2 occurred in August to September in the hypertrophic period and from July to October during the eutrophic period.

In the hypertrophic phase, SRP concentrations usually fell below 10 lg P L⁻¹ during April and May (Fig. 2). In the transient phase, the periods with low SRP concentration tended to start earlier in March and were already finished by May. In the eutrophic phase, the centroid of the period with SRP < 10 lg L⁻¹ occurred some weeks later. The time of this centroid (tlow SRP, expressed as elapsed time in weeks since 1 March) can be described by the regression:

Correspondingly low concentrations of dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN < 72 lg L⁻¹ as defined by the Redfield ratio of N : P = 7.2 by weight) did not occur before 1985, but were very frequent during the transient period and became recurrent summer events in the eutrophic period (Fig. 2). Nitrate contributed about 85% to DIN in spring and 55% in summer.

Shifts towards higher surface water temperatures were observed around 1988 (winter/spring) and around 1991 (summer). On average, mean air temperatures in winter and in April/May were about 1–5 °C higher in 1988–98 than in 1979–87. At the same time, surface water temperatures increased by 0.5–2 °C. Mean ice cover duration decreased from 60 ± 23 days in 1976–87 to 38 ± 31 days in 1988–2002. The mean date of ice-out was March 12 ± 10 days and February 16 ± 26 days, respectively. Mean summer surface water temperatures were 0.5–2 °C higher in 1991–98 than in 1979–90.

In winter (November to February), mean phytoplankton biovolume decreased from 5.9 ± 3.5 mm³ L⁻¹ in 1981–90 to 3.6 ± 1.8 in 1991–96 and to 1.7 ± 1.5 mm³ L⁻¹ in 1997–2003. The onset of the spring diatom bloom depended mainly on the duration of ice cover. The biovolume of diatoms (BVdiatoms) in March was inversely related to the date of ice-out (tice in Julian days): BVdiatoms = 21.2 − 0.26tice r² = 0.53; n = 22; P < 0.001: However, this effect did not persist into April. The timing of the spring phytoplankton maximum did not change significantly during the transient and eutrophic phases (P = 0.72), but a significant negative trend was observed during the hypertrophic period (P = 0.001).

Under hypertrophic conditions, phytoplankton reached a mean total biovolume of 17.4 mm³ L⁻¹ in spring (March to May) and 15.9 mm³ L⁻¹ in summer (June to September). By the eutrophic period, the mean biovolume had declined to 4.2 (spring) and 7.2 mm³ L⁻¹ (summer, see Fig. 3). In spring, mean phytoplankton biovolumes were highly correlated with TP concentration (Fig. 4) and global radiation (r² = 0.45, P = 0.001). In summer, mean phytoplankton biovolumes were correlated with global radiation (r² = 0.35, P = 0.004) and mean TN concentration (Fig. 4), but also with the mean concentrations of TP and TN in the previous spring (P < 0.05). Seasonal means of phytoplankton biovolume were not correlated with water temperature.

The mean proportion (±SD) of total phytoplankton biovolume accounted for by cyanobacteria decreased from 19 ± 7% (1981–90) to 6.5 ± 3.1% (1991–96) and to 3.6 ± 3.3% (1997–2003) in the spring, but did not change significantly in the summer (54 ± 18% in 1980–90 and 48 ± 24% in 1997–2003). In the hypertrophic period, spring diatoms were joined each April by the filamentous cyanobacterium Limnothrix redekei (van Goor) Meffert. A L. redekei bloom was often succeeded immediately by a bloom of Planktothrix agardhii (Gomont) Anagn. et Komarek, which then dominated or co-dominated the phytoplankton during the whole of the following summer, although in some years (1979, 1982, 1985, 1990), Aphanizomenon flos-aquae (L.) Ralfs ex Born. et Flah. and Microcystis spp. dominated after a short clear-water phase. In the 1990s, however, both L. redekei and P. agardhii disappeared almost completely and the spring bloom was always terminated by a more distinct clear-water phase. The mean biovolume of the N₂-fixing cyanobacterium A. flos-aquae remained constant. This species has dominated the summer phytoplankton in recent years.

Compared with the hypertrophic period, mean abundances of Daphnia spp. remained nearly constant in spring. During summer, however, they declined by 38% in the transient and by 60% in the eutrophic period. The mean rotifer fresh biomass declined by 46% in the transient and by 21% in the eutrophic period in spring and increased by 20% and by 61% in summer, respectively.

german_name.evidence_anchor: Große Teile der Bundeswasserstraßen liegen in Schutzgebieten nach nationalem und europäischem Naturschutzrecht. Auf Grund der erheblichen Nutzungsintensität der Bundeswasserstraßen z. B. zu Zwecken der Schif ahrt, der Wasserkraftnutzung, der Urbanisierung und aus Hochwasserschutzgründen können sie diese Funktionen in der Regel nicht mehr erfüllen. Um die genannten Nutzungen zu ermöglichen, sind die ursprünglichen Fluss- und Auenlandschaften tiefgreifend verändert worden. Die Flüsse wurden begradigt und mittels Buhnen und Längsbauwerken, die aus massiven Steinschüttungen bestehen, in einen festgelegten Lauf gezwungen. Die daraus folgende Tiefenerosion und Hochwasserschutzmaßnahmen haben die Auen von den Flüssen entkoppelt und größtenteils von dem Überflutungsgeschehen des Flusses abgeschnitten. Diese Flächen werden heute landwirtschaftlich genutzt. Nur 6 % der Bundeswasserstraßen weisen eine Struktur- oder Lebensraumausstattung auf, die als „unverändert bis mäßig verändert“ und daher noch als naturnah bezeichnet werden kann. Some possible reasons for this might be that diverse wild pollinators provide a better pollination, for example through greater cross-pollination (Garibaldi et al., 2013; Woodcock et al., 2013), higher efficiency of pollination by complementarity of their foraging behavior (i.e., niche complementarity; Brittain et al., 2013a), or through positive effects of some pollinators on the pollination function of other pollinators (i.e., functional facilitation; Greenleaf and Kremen, 2006; Klein et al., 2009).

We used two modelling approaches to quantify the effect of tree diversity on individual tree and plot level growth. At the individual tree level, our objectives were to quantify the effect of diversity and competitive interactions on individual tree growth, whilst accounting for tree size and local topography. At the stand level, our objectives were to quantify the effects of stand diversity on the joint performance of different species.

biodiversity_level.evidence_anchor: Die wuchsschwachen Fadenbinsen-Wiesen sind niedrig (50-70 cm) und fallen durch dichte Herden bürstiger Binsenhalme auf. Die Auswirkungen eines so frühen Mahdzeitpunkts auf die Artenzusammensetzung sind aber nicht bekannt.

Aufgrund der ausgeprägten Abhängigkeit der Artenzusammensetzung von Brenndolden - Auenwiesen von den hydrologischen Bedingungen sind Eingriffe in den Wasserhaushalt immer hoch problematisch im Sinne des Naturschutzes und daher generell zu vermeiden.

biodiversity_level.evidence_anchor: reduzieren Schwermetalle das Wachstum von Organismen, ändern die morphologische Struktur oder hemmen biochemische Prozesse der einzelnen Zellen. Bodentiere nehmen Schwermetalle durch die Haut und mit der Nahrung auf. Bei Regenwürmern wird ein großer Anteil der Schwermetalle in die Cuticula eingelagert. Innerhalb der Nahrungskette führt dies zu einer Bioakkumulation von Schwermetallen. Die Toxizität von Schwermetallen ist bei unterschiedlichen Bodenorganismen unterschiedlich stark ausgeprägt. In der unteren Auenstufe dominiert Silberweidenwald (nival geprägt: oberhalb der Mittelwasserlinie, pluvial: unterhalb), auf der Höheren Eichen-Ulmenwald. Lokale Vorkommen von trockenen, offenen Sandflächen (Dünen) mit Sandtrockenrasen und stark austrocknende Kiesflächen (Brennen) mit Magerrasen treten auf.

Zo is bekend dat beweiding door grote grazers kan zorgen voor compactie van de bodem, waardoor afbraakprocessen langzamer gaan en de koolstoffvoorraad hierdoor mogelijk groter wordt (Elschot _et al.,_ 2015).

Het door compactie beïnvloeden van de abiotische omstandigheden in de bodem (zoals zuurstofbeschikbaarheid en vochtgehalte) was in dat onderzoek de belangrijkste oorzaak van de lagere koolstoffafbraak. Er is echter ook onderzoek waarbij de effecten van beweiding minimaal waren (Harvey _et al_ ., 2019).

german_name.evidence_anchor: The range of species observed in our study is not limited to widespread epiphytic bryophytes, but we have also detected numerous species of conservation concern. Even a few years after their first detection, some of these species can no longer be described as rare. We found Orthotrichum pulchellum, first recorded in the Erzgebirge in 2002 (Seifert and Nixdorf 2002), in almost every Sorbus, Fagus and Acer plot, O. rogeri and Cryphaea heteromalla in almost 60% and O. scanicum in 50% of the Acer plots examined. Meinunger and Schroder (2007) described an increase in population size and range of O. pulchellum in Germany already 15 years ago. Furthermore, occurrences of O. rogeri and C. heteromalla have now even been documented in urban areas (Richter et al. 2009; Stebel and Fojcik 2016). However, in our study, the overwhelming number of occurrences of species of conservation concern is the discovery of a single cushion or patch. The only exception is O. pulchellum, which has large populations in some plots. Larger occurrences of other species of conservation concern, as reported by Lüth (2010) and Eckstein et al. (2020) for O. rogeri, were not found in the Erzgebirge. With regard to the threatened status of these species, Seifert (2009) has already discussed this problem in detail. The numerous finds of new species (species group 1 and 2) suggest that in addition to the decline in S deposits, other environmental factors also influence the current development of the species composition of epiphytic bryophytes. Until a few decades ago, the distribution of some of these species in Central Europe was largely limited to coastal areas, e.g. Cryphaea heteromalla (submediterran-subatlantic distribution) and Orthotrichum pulchellum (oceanic-temperate distribution). Their current spread is associated with positive temperature anomalies in winter (Frahm and Klaus 2001). Another factor that could explain the spread of epiphytic bryophytes is the atmospheric deposition of nitrogen (N). Most of the newly found epiphytic bryophytes are classified with N values between “5” (moderately N rich sites, e.g. Orthotrichum scanicum) and “7” (N rich sites, e.g. Cryphaea heteromalla) (Simmel et al., 2021). The records of Ulota drummondii and Neckera pennata in this study after a long period of absence also corroborate this conclusion.

german_name.evidence_anchor: Wegen der Abnahme extensiver Weiden sind viele koprophage Insekten inzwischen hochgradig gefährdet. Nur großflächige Weidelandschaften mit langer Weidetradition können die volle Artengemeinschaft der Dungkäfer (ca. 100 Arten sind obligate Dungbewohner) und der von ihnen abhängigen Arten entwickeln (Buse et al. 2014). Und selbst wenn Dung auf Weideflächen heute noch vorhanden ist, kann dieser auf produktionsorientierten Flächen zur Falle für viele Insekten werden: Der Dung heutiger Nutztierweiden kann, je nach Behandlungszeitraum und -mittel, durch ausgeschiedene Medikamente (z. B. Avermectine) und/oder deren Metabolite letal auf die Entwicklung von Insektenlarven wirken. Derartige Behandlungen unterbinden damit den Aufbau von Destruentenzönosen (Laurence 1954; Mackenzie, Oxford 1995; Madsen et al. 1990). Wilde Weiden besitzen ein hohes Potenzial, um die hochdiverse, direkt und indirekt vom Dung abhängige Fauna zu fördern, da hier kein ökonomischer Nutzungsanspruch vorliegt und entsprechend wenig/keine Behandlung erforderlich ist bzw. diese auch im Sinne nachfolgender Weide-Zönosen durchgeführt werden kann (Jay-Robert et al. 2008; Sandom et al. 2014; Waßmer 1995).
